entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2) Learned Counsel for the Petitioners submits that one Motilal Shrivastava had filed a claim petition under Section 110(A) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 for the accidental death of his son before the First Additional Motor Accidental Claims Tribunal, Raipur where the same was registered as Claim Case No. 165/91, wherein, an award was passed on 29/08/1997 granting amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.1,10,000/- which was to be payable by the non-applicants No.1 and 2.

entities.text: First Additional Motor Accidental Claims Tribunal, Raipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is contended further that being aggrieved with the said award, an appeal was preferred by said Motilal Shrivastava, registered as M.A. No.1529/1997, before the erstwhile High Court of Madhya Pradesh and after the formation of State of Chhattisgarh, it was transferred to this Court.
The said appeal was however, dismissed on 20/04/2007 for want of prosecution by the Division Bench of this Court.

3) It is contended further that since said Motilal Shrivastava was died on 15/02/2000, prior to the dismissal of the said appeal, therefore, the legal representatives of him filed a petition for its restoration, which was registered as MCC No. 519/2013.

The said petition was dismissed by this Court vide order dated 24/12/2014 whereby, a liberty was granted to the legal representatives to take an appropriate steps as required under Order 22 Rule 9 of CPC and, in pursuance thereof,
another petition, being MCC No.331/2017 was filed by the legal representatives of said deceased Motilal Shrivastava on 07/03/2017 for the restoration of the said appeal, alongwith an application under Order 22 Rule 9 of CPC, but since, it was filed without invoking the power to condone the delay for setting aside the abatement, therefore, it was dismissed vide order dated 01/05/2017.

It is contended further that since it was dismissed without prejudice to the right of the petitioners,
therefore, the instant petition has been filed for setting aside the abatement of the said appeal,
alongwith an application for its condonation of delay as provided under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.

4) According to the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners, since the aforesaid petitions, i.e.
MCC No. 519 of 2013 and MCC No. 331 of 2017 have been filed due to the ill advise of the counsel,
though the petitioners are continuously pursuing for restoration of the said appeal and as there is no malafide and/or ulterior motive of the petitioners for filing of this petition, therefore, the delay which has been occurred bonafidely may kindly be condoned in the interest of justice.

5) It, however, appears from perusal of the record that the original appellant namely Motilal Shrivastava being aggrieved with the award dated 29/08/1997 passed in Claim Case No.165/1991 had preferred an appeal which was registered as M.A. No.1529/1997.

The said appeal was dismissed on non-prosecution vide order dated 20/04/2007 and for its restoration, the proposed legal representatives of said original appellant have filed a petition, being MCC No.519/2013, which was dismissed vide order dated 24/12/2014, while observing at para 2 as under :-
"2.

As per Annexure A/1, sole applicant Motilal Shrivastava died on 15.2.2000 i.e.
before passing of the order in question, in these circumstances, present MCC in the form of restoration of MA dismissed for want of prosecution is not maintainable and dismissed as not maintainable reserving liberty to legal representatives to appellant Motilal Shrivastava (Dead) Through Lrs vs The Raipur Transport Co. Pvt. Ltd on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85995696/
2
Motilal Shrivastava to take appropriate steps may be under Order 22 Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
No order as to costs."

6) It appears that even after the liberty was granted as above, no petition as required was moved immediately thereafter, but instead another petition, being MCC No.331/2017 was filed for restoration of the said appeal i.e. M.A. No.1529/1997, alongwith an application for setting aside the abatement as provided under Order 22 of CPC.

The said petition has been dismissed vide order dated 01/05/2017 while observing at paras 3 and 4 as under:-
"3.

Instead of invoking the power to condone delay in applying to set aside the abatement and seeking the relief to set aside the abatement and also for consequential impleadment through interlocutory applications in M.A. No.1529 of 1997, the legal representatives of Motilal Shrivastava, since deceased, have filed this MCC as if it is a composite proceedings.
We have to ensure that due process is followed.
It is obviously means that due procedure prescribed by the laws are to be adhered to.

4. Under such circumstances, this MCC is dismissed without prejudice to the Applicants' rights, if any, to apply through interlocutory applications in M.A. No.1529 of 1997 for condonation of delay in applying to set aside the abatement; to set aside the abatement; and, for impleadment of the legal representatives of Late Motilal Shrivastava.
We clarify that we have not mentioned anything on the merits of any such of applications."

7) Despite the aforesaid observations being made no step was, however, taken immediately thereafter and, instead, the instant petition has been filed much after passing of the considerable period of more than 6 years even without assigning any cogent and reliable reasons as to why,
they approach this Court for such a long delay, although the liberties were granted, as reflected from the orders passed on 24/12/2024 and 01/05/2024 in MCC No.519 of 2013 and MCC No.331 of 2017,
respectively.
8) In view of the aforesaid background, we are not inclined to condone the delay of 6143 days in filing of this petition.
The said application is, accordingly, rejected and consequently, the petition as framed stands dismissed.

No order as to cost(s).
 -Sd/- -Sd/-
 (Goutam Bhaduri) (Sanjay S. Agrawal)
